message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  zig:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Update packages list
        run: sudo apt-get update

      - name: Install Zig
        uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2
        with:
          version: master

      - name: Build
        run: |
          zig build
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-windows
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos
          zig build -Dtarget=wasm32-freestanding
          zig build -Drelease
          rm -fr zig-cache zig-out        
       
  make:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Update packages list
        run: sudo apt-get update

      - name: Install Make
        run: sudo apt-get install make

      - name: Build
        run: make

      - name: Test
        run: make test
       
",
  "rationale": "Add a custom timeout of 5 minutes to each job to prevent runaway builds. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern and its experiment examples show elapsed time savings of 9-26% with no false timeouts for jobs of similar duration. The workflow's historical successful runs complete within ~2 minutes, so 5 minutes provides ample headroom while bounding resource consumption.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  zig:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Update packages list
        run: sudo apt-get update

      - name: Install Zig
        uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2
        with:
          version: master

      - name: Build
        run: |
          zig build
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-windows
          zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos
          zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos
          zig build -Dtarget=wasm32-freestanding
          zig build -Drelease
          rm -fr zig-cache zig-out       
      
  make:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Update packages list
        run: sudo apt-get update

      - name: Install Make
        run: sudo apt-get install make

      - name: Build
        run: make

      - name: Test
        run: make test

Now, rationale: We add a custom timeout of 5 minutes to each job to prevent runaway builds, based on evidence from P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern and experiment examples showing elapsed time savings of 9-26% with no false timeouts for similar job durations. The workflow's historical successful runs complete within ~2 minutes, so 5 minutes provides ample headroom.
